newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank to release revaluation profits in 98.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank to release revaluation profits in 98.

text.p: Sources in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's ruling coalition said on Tuesday the Bundesbank and the German government had agreed to revalue its gold and currency reserves at the end of 1997, but would only transfer profits to Bonn in 1998.

"The result will have an effect from 1997 to 1998, and in that way we are coming to an agreed solution," the sources told reporters after a meeting between Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer.

Kohl's coalition backed down earlier on Tuesday on a controversial plan to revalue central bank assets after parliamentary deputies from Kohl's party sharply criticised the proposal aimed at helping Germany plug budget gaps.

Another source in the ruling coalition said protests from conservative Christian Democrats (CDU) deputies had forced the coalition to retreat from the plan to revalue central bank reserves to help Germany qualify for European monetary union (EMU).
"A solution is only possible with support of the Bundesbank," the coalition source told Reuters. "In face of the resistance from the Bundesbank, the revaluation for 1997 is no longer on the table."

Abandoning the plan to revalue the assets will mean that there is another 10 billion mark ($5.8 billion) hole in the 1997 budget, the official said. To fill that hole, the coalition was discussing privatisations, budget cuts and moderate tax increases.
